## A repository on a slide

A ` ```git-sandbox ` block works on a slide like anywhere else. On a slide
there is less room, so the next one leaves out the editor and the commit
tree and offers only two of the views below the terminal; the chevron at
the end of their tabs folds them away.

Source code and issues:
[github.com/jansim/quarto-git-sandbox](https://github.com/jansim/quarto-git-sandbox).
The [author's guide](example.html) explains every option.

## Make a first commit

```git-sandbox
id: deck-repo
title: Start a project
prompt: "~/slides-demo $"
editor: false
tree-view: false
panel-tabs: [files, history]
intro: |
  An empty folder. Make it a repository and commit a file.
tasks:
  - text: Turn the folder into a repository with `git init`
    when: repo
  - text: Create a file, stage it and commit it
    when: commits >= 1
```

## Meanwhile, on a later slide

```git-sandbox
id: deck-branch
share: deck-repo
title: Branch and merge, same repository
editor: false
tree-view: true
panels: false
intro: |
  This is the repository from the previous slide, commits and all.
  Branch off, commit, and merge back; the tree on the right follows.
tasks:
  - text: Create and switch to a branch called `idea`
    when: on idea
  - text: Commit on `idea`
    when: commits on idea >= 2
  - text: Go back to `main` and merge `idea`
    when: on main and merged idea into main
```

## How the second slide was written

`share` points a box at an earlier exercise's repository. The view has
its own title, tasks and layout, and no `seed`: the repository comes from
the box it shares.

````markdown
```git-sandbox
id: deck-branch
share: deck-repo
title: Branch and merge, same repository
editor: false
tree-view: true
panels: false
tasks:
  - text: Create and switch to a branch called `idea`
    when: on idea
```
````

Typing in a box does not move the slides: reveal.js leaves keys alone
while the terminal has focus. Click outside the box to navigate again.
